subtype: Approach: reviewing after a broken agreement [Revision]
passage: Bhupen reached the village at nine that night, an hour after he should have. The cricket match in the next village had gone into extra overs, and he had not phoned from Ramu's shop. His mother Uma was standing at the gate with a torch. She said nothing at first. Bhupen took a breath. "Amma, I lost track of the time. I could have called from the shop and I didn't. I have no excuse." Uma folded her arms, but her shoulders came down a little. "So, what now?" "For two weeks I'll ring from the shop by six every evening and be home by seven. If I miss a call, you can keep me in." Uma nodded slowly. "Two weeks. We'll see." The next day Bhupen rang at ten to six.

qa.q: How late was Bhupen coming home?
qa.a: Bhupen was an hour late, reaching the village at nine.

qa.q: What might Bhupen be feeling when saying 'I have no excuse'?
qa.a: Bhupen is probably guilty and nervous but sincere, since he owns up before being asked and offers a fix.

qa.q: What else could Bhupen do to rebuild trust, and why?
qa.a: Bhupen could keep the calls steady for all two weeks and be on time each day, because repeated proof is what repairs trust.

qa.q: How does Uma see waiting at the gate?
qa.a: Uma was worried while waiting, then softened once Bhupen owned up, which is why her shoulders came down.

grounding: After coming home late once, the teen owns up, explains without excuses and proposes a stricter check-in for two weeks, showing that trust can be repaired.

passage: Sofia's curfew in Seville was ten, and she walked through the door at 10:50. Her father, Javier, was sitting in the hall in his coat, phone in hand. Before he could speak, she said, "I'm sorry. I'm late, and I didn't call. That's on me." He waited. "We missed the last tram because I wanted to stay for one more song. Then my phone died. That's the reason, but it's not an excuse." Javier took off his coat slowly. "I was about to go looking for you." "I know. So here's what I want to do: for the next two weekends I'll text you every hour, and I'll be home by half past nine, not ten. I'll carry a power bank. Then we can see." Her father looked at her for a long moment. "Every hour," he said. "And the power bank."

qa.q: What time did Sofia get home?
What was Sofia feeling when she spoke before her father could?
qa.a: She felt guilty and wanted to own up straight away rather than wait to be scolded.

qa.q: Why did Sofia's response help repair trust?
qa.a: She apologised without excuses, explained honestly and offered a stricter check-in for two weeks, showing she took his worry seriously.

qa.q: How was Javier feeling, sitting in the hall in his coat?
qa.a: He was worried and anxious, about to go out looking for her.

grounding: Shows a teen who came home late owning up, explaining without excuses and proposing a stricter two-week check-in to repair trust.

passage: In the warden's office of the boarding school, Raghav held the landline receiver with both hands. He had signed back in at 7:40; the rule his parents had agreed with the school was 6:30. Arnab Sir had already called home. "Mummy, Papa, I'm sorry," Raghav said. "I was late. We lost track of time at the market, and I didn't call. There's no good excuse." Silence on the line, then Papa: "We were very worried, Raghav." "I know. For the next two weeks I'll sign out only with Arnab Sir's okay and phone you from the office when I'm back. If I'm even five minutes late, no outings for a month." Arnab Sir raised his eyebrows. After a pause, Mummy said, "Two weeks. Then we talk again." Raghav let out a long breath.

qa.q: What time did Raghav sign back in?
What does Raghav holding the receiver with both hands suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt nervous and ashamed about facing his parents.

qa.q: Why is proposing his own stricter rule a good step?
qa.a: It shows he takes the lateness seriously and gives his parents a clear way to watch trust being rebuilt.

qa.q: How did Papa feel about the late return?
qa.a: Papa was very worried, as he says on the phone.

grounding: Shows a teen owning up to a late return, giving the reason without excuses and proposing a stricter two-week check-in.
